items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: And old Joe Steele would be in there.

ctx.x: he was a gambling musician, a musician who gambled, and... That was part of their life, too. They could, you know, sit down. You've got that kind of patience, you know, to sit down for hours and gamble. And they would gamble, because they... They was gamblers!

And he opened this club, and he called it the Rhythm Club. And naturally, the musicians began to come around. And they had a piano in there, always well-tuned. It was a baby grand. And they didn't allow you to just noodle on it. You had to be able to play something, or they'd tell you, "Don't mess with that instrument. Get up from there unless you can play something." And old Joe Steele would be in there. Sammy Stewart would be in there. That other piano player...
Sammy Stewart was a piano player.
